title: A Drone Killed Three Ukrainians. It Was Guided Entirely by A.I.
partialText: An attack by what Ukrainian officials said was a Russian drone with an Nvidia chip presages a dystopian future of weaponry untethered to humans.

title: Some of Russia’s A.I. Drones Are Powered by Nvidia Microcomputers, Ukrainian Officials Say
partialText: The tech giant says it does not sell the devices in Russia, but they are widely available on resale markets. When purchased that way, they are virtually impossible to track.

title: UK Prime Minister Burnham Arrives in Ukraine as Russia Amps Up Warnings
partialText: In his first foreign trip since taking office, Prime Minister Andy Burnham affirmed support for Kyiv despite new warnings from Moscow of potential consequences.

title: U.S. to Unveil ‘Economic D-Day’ Sanctions Targeting Iran’s Economy
partialText: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will hold a news conference outlining the new package of measures.

title: Iran Cracks Down on One Luxury Left to Its Youth: Coffee Shops
partialText: In recent weeks, the police have closed dozens of cafes, often citing laws that stipulate women must veil in public. Experts say the closures are part of an effort to control public space.

title: Iran Pledges to Defy Trump’s Economic Sanctions
partialText: Analysts say Tehran could intensify the dispute militarily after attempts to squeeze its economy. An Iranian official vowed “not a single drop of oil” would leave the Gulf.

title: Oil Prices Fall Ahead of U.S. Vow to Intensify Economic War Against Iran
partialText: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to announce an escalation of sanctions aimed at further isolating Iranian trade.

title: Farmers Struggle to Get Basic Services From Depleted Agriculture Dept.
partialText: After the departure of thousands of federal workers, rural communities report problems obtaining loans, grants, technical assistance and support for infrastructure and other services.

title: In West Texas, Trump’s Border Wall Collides With Latino History
partialText: A century ago, Mexican American families came together to build an adobe church near the border. Can its bell toll again as the wall expansion nears?

title: U.S. Military Kills 2 People in Attack on Boat in Pacific
partialText: The United States has killed at least 223 people since its campaign of boat strikes began nearly a year ago.

title: Can Democrats Win Back the Senate? Why Their Chances Are Improving.
partialText: Republicans still have some clear advantages on the map, but President Trump’s unpopularity has opened the door for an outcome that once seemed far-fetched.

title: With Trump Against Him, Can Ralph Norman Win in South Carolina?
partialText: The ultraconservative congressman who has broken with the president on spending is hoping voters reward his experience, contrarian streak and all.

title: Eon Huntley, the Democratic Socialist Running for Office While Working at Bergdorf
partialText: For Eon Huntley, who won his primary in New York in June, good clothes and populist policies go together.

title: How Should ‘Huckleberry Finn’ Be Taught?
partialText: I traveled around the country to find out if “Adventures of Huckleberry Finn” still has a place in the classroom.

title: More Companies Are Promising Cloud Seeding Can Make Rain
partialText: States are spending millions of dollars on cloud seeding technology, backed by new data on its effectiveness — and driven by desperation for water.

title: The Woman Guiding Tourists Through New York City’s Worst Day
partialText: Christina Stanton offers a very specific and deeply personal tour of the World Trade Center site to remind visitors what happened 25 years ago.

title: The Ruthless Efficiency of Ultrapotent Street Drugs
partialText: Five decades after the “war on drugs” sought to make substance abuse unaffordable, illicit drugs are cheaper and more powerful than ever. A visit to Baltimore shows why.

title: Why Getting High Has Only Gotten Cheaper
partialText: The “war on drugs” sought to reduce substance abuse by driving up prices and lowering demand. Today, street drugs are less expensive and more dangerous than ever.

title: Washington Post Ordered to Rehire Fired Columnist Karen Attiah
partialText: An arbitrator ordered the newspaper to reinstate Karen Attiah, who was fired after posting about “white men who espouse hatred and violence” following Charlie Kirk’s killing.

title: Research Firm’s Founder Explains $6 Million Payment to Fired Forbes Editor
partialText: RJ Shook of Shook Research said he paid Randall Lane, the former top editor at Forbes, for “services and guidance” in partnering with Forbes and later selling his research firm.

title: After Hugging Face Was Attacked By A.I. Agents, It Embarked on a Crusade
partialText: Hugging Face, a start-up that was breached by rogue bots from OpenAI, is using the hack to push for openness in A.I. development.

title: Anatomy of an Autonomous Attack: 5 Alarming A.I. Capabilities
partialText: When OpenAI’s agents went rogue in July, they demonstrated ingenuity and drive beyond what many experts imagined — a dangerous harbinger of what such bots could do in the future.

title: These Conservatives Want to Be Working Moms. The Manosphere Disapproves.
partialText: At a conservative center for women leaders, interns told stories about their lives. One said a male classmate told her, “I don’t know if women should be lawyers.”

title: We’re in a New Era of Class Warfare. History Points to a Way Out.
partialText: The class-based violence of the past was part of a broader struggle. Today, the violence is the end in itself.

title: Canada Said No to America. It Will Reverberate Far Beyond Its Borders.
partialText: Mark Carney has chosen suffering, but he did what Canadians elected him to do.

title: Should We Read ‘Huck Finn’?
partialText: One reporter traveled to understand how it is taught now.

title: Fast-Moving Reno Wildfire Forces Thousands to Evacuate in Nevada
partialText: The Hawk fire has burned more than 15,000 acres since it began on Saturday in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada near Reno.
